q: Which phase follows schematic design?
n: Design development follows schematic design: schematic design → design development → contract documents. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: What is the architect's responsibility when checking materials and completed work to ensure conformance with specifications?
n: Checking materials and completed work against the specifications is part of project supervision by the architect. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (construction phase).

q: In which part of the architect's services do site utilization and feasibility studies fall?
n: Site utilization and feasibility studies fall under pre-design services. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: In which phase do the architect and client choose the contractor?
n: The contractor is chosen in the bidding or negotiation phase, when bids are evaluated and the contract awarded. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: In a bidding, what is the role of the architect?
o: Award the project to the contractor
n: In bidding the architect organizes the process: invitations, bid documents, bid opening and evaluation. The owner makes the award. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (bidding phase).

q: What is the foremost role of the architect between the client and contractor?
o: To execute judicial orders with impartiality
n: Between client and contractor the architect acts first as impartial mediator, interpreting the contract documents fairly for both sides. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: What is the foremost role of an architect with regards to his client?
n: To the client the architect is foremost an adviser, giving independent professional counsel on design, cost and construction. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the client).

q: Who orients the contractor on the contract documents?
o: No one; it's the contractor's job
n: The architect orients the contractor on the contract documents and interprets them. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions).

q: Who is responsible for asking for a final inspection of a project?
n: The contractor requests the final inspection when it considers the work complete. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); AIA A201 Sec. 9.10.

q: When the architect checks materials and work against the specifications, this is:
n: Checking materials and work against the specifications is construction supervision or inspection, not drawing estimates, quality control or contract surveying, so none of the choices fits. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: Who is responsible for damage and accidents on site?
n: The contractor controls the site and is responsible for damage and accidents there, including safety under OSHS. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); DOLE OSHS (RA 11058).

q: In which phase does the architect decide claims of owner and contractor about the work and the contract documents?
n: In the construction phase the architect decides claims and disputes between owner and contractor about the work and the contract documents. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: What drawings record the changes made during construction?
n: As-built plans record the changes made during construction. They are submitted on completion. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 309.

q: As business development manager, the architect shall:
o: Compare the design program with actual use
n: As business development manager, the architect devises schemes to reach maximum occupancy of the building. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: What is the method of compensation when there is a continuity of a relationship on a series of projects?
n: For a continuing relationship over a series of projects, professional fee plus expenses is the usual method. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: A full-time inspector engaged by the owner works under whose technical control?
n: A full-time inspector engaged by the owner works under the technical direction of the architect. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A.

q: What do you call the architect after construction?
n: After construction, an architect retained for post-construction services acts as a consulting architect. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.1.2.

q: The architect may be engaged as ______ of a building or complex to extend its life and maximize economic return.
n: The architect may be engaged as building administrator or property manager to extend the building's life and maximize its economic return. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: How is a building administrator paid?
o: A percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees and/or a monthly fee
n: A building administrator is paid a percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees, or a monthly fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.

q: Role of architect after being hired by the owner in post-construction.
n: Hired by the owner after construction, the architect serves as a design consultant on alterations, use and maintenance (post-construction services). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: After a hospital is built, whom should the client hire for building maintenance?
o: An architect with a track record in building and equipment maintenance
n: For hospital maintenance, hire an architect with a proven track record in building and equipment maintenance. Relevant experience matters. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: What does the contractor hand over after completion to help the building run properly?
n: At completion the contractor hands over the building operations and maintenance manuals, with warranties, so the building runs properly. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); CSI MasterFormat Div. 01 78 23.

q: Which service keeps the structure, plumbing and electrical systems in good condition?
n: Building maintenance keeps the structure, plumbing and electrical systems in good condition. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: Which service keeps entrances, exits, parking, walkways and ramps orderly?
n: Grounds and landscaping supervision keeps entrances, exits, parking, walkways and ramps orderly. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: Which service sees that third parties keep all equipment properly maintained?
n: Equipment maintenance sees that third parties keep all equipment properly maintained. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: Which service devises schemes to reach maximum occupancy?
n: Business development devises schemes to reach maximum occupancy. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205.

q: This scientific study allows the architect to focus on the ways in which the building can best maintain itself and prolong its life.
n: Forensic architecture is the scientific study of how a building has performed or failed, which shows how it can best maintain itself and prolong its life. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 209 (allied services).

q: Which service covers materials, construction methods, envelopes, roofing, finishes, hardware and fittings?
n: Building components services cover materials, construction methods, building envelopes, roofing, finishes, hardware and fittings. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, UAP SPP Doc. 209 (allied services).

q: Knowledge of office operations, management, accounting, finance and taxation falls under:
n: Office operations, management, accounting, finance and taxation fall under management of architectural practice. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 200 series; RA 9266 IRR.

q: Which service ensures a building's systems are planned, installed and tested to perform as designed?
n: Building commissioning verifies that a building's systems are planned, installed and tested to perform as designed. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines; ASHRAE Guideline 0 (Commissioning Process).

q: Eight-hour daily site supervision falls under which service?
n: Eight-hour daily site supervision by the architect's representative is full-time supervision, a separate service with its own fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A (Full-Time Supervision).

q: What does building appraisal do?
o: Checks if it was well designed
n: Building appraisal estimates the value of a building or property. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (allied services); Appraisal Institute.

q: Which service plans light transmission, timing and control to suit the design concept?
n: Architectural lighting layout and design plans light distribution, timing and control to suit the design concept. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (allied services); IES Lighting Handbook.

q: In which area does the architect recommend methods for sustainable, green design?
n: Building environment certification has the architect recommend sustainable, green design methods and guide the project through rating systems (BERDE, LEED). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (allied services); PHILGBC BERDE.

q: Which area rates and secures structures so work can be carried out safely and protected?
n: Security evaluation and planning assesses and secures structures so they can be used and maintained safely and protected. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (allied services).

q: What is the recommended fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) for a gymnasium with a PCC of ₱50 million or less?
n: For a gymnasium (Group 3, exceptional complexity) with a project construction cost of ₱50 million or less, the recommended fee for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services is 7% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.3 (Group 3 fee schedule).
